open_points: 2.15.1 says two cars and two drivers at rung 1; no source says which car each drives or when Tom takes one. Shifts (Kevin 07:00-19:00 on car one, Terry 19:00-03:00 on car two, Tom takes the idle one) are chosen.
Rung 2 to 5: car three at rung 2 and cars four and five at rung 3 are slots filled at purchase from the lot or a seller; no source says what the sellers' cars are.
The lot's stock is fixed seven cars; nothing says it restocks.
New plates have no price in any source; the respray price (£90) is the prototype's, not the economy file's.
The ambulance livery (white with an orange band) is UNVERIFIED for 1990; the art keeper must check.

Parked-car kit: only the two kept places (street-vehicles.json) come from a source; the other eleven places are chosen, moved 0.7 and 1.1 m up Quay Street so the first two clear Mickey's rank (s 9.5 to 14.5) as the brief requires.
Plate year letters on parked and traffic cars are chosen; the fleet's E412 is the prototype's.
The milk float and the bus are chosen scenery; 4.6.2 names neither (RULINGS 23 Sep makes buses scenery; a milk float is a 1990 sight).
Boot slots: GV-01 names three things (envelope, spare coat, box) but no count; three item slots and one body slot are chosen.
A stop's 'steering lock' flag by registration year is a chosen rule; no source gives which cars have one.
fictional_note: every make and model is invented (canon: no real car models); a look-alike check against real makes is owed at the art gate (4.6.1). No brand, badge, crest or logo is shown; the maker's plate is left blank (brand-bible).
